articles.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
articles.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.
points: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates.

articles.title: Jobs digest: moves and promotions at Supercell, Scopely, EA, Mattel, Tripledot, Zynga, Tencent and more
articles.summary: Our jobs digest has all the recruitment news you need from across the mobile games business, all in one spot. This column is sponsored by FastSpring. FastSpring: Global payments for your games from a partner you can trust with your players.
body: Supercell: Kimmo Frisk has joined as central QA specialist, having previous served in QA roles at Wiztivi Gaming and Iceflake Studios. Former Mediatonic, Fortis, and Tripledot artist Vittorio Durin has joined as senior technical artist, working on an unannounced project. Yana Brusynska joins as DevOps engineer on the server infra team, and former HiRez and Riot artists Hans Hirth has begun a new role as Supercell’s 3D artist and art outsource manager.

Tomás González Saavedra also joins as a senior product manager for live ops on the Clash Royale team, covering a paternity leave contract role in Helsinki. He has previously held product management roles at Yodo1, Tilting Point and Gamehouse.

Scopely: Former King talent manager Albert Casas has joined the global talent acquisition team at the Monopoly Go maker. Tara Durbha joins as associate game designer on Bingo Bash, while Cory Taylor joins as senior community manager on an unannounced upcoming title, having moved over from Warner Bros Games.
EA: Nick Nyaiesh has taken on a new role at EA as game product manager, where he’ll be focused on EA’s American football mobile games. He joined EA in 2024 as associate game designer.

articles.title: “How did we misjudge this so badly…?” What Supercell learned from upsetting Clash Royale players
articles.summary: Game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell talked through Clash Royale player drama and how to deal with it at Gamescom Dev.
body: Supercell explained some of the thinking behind several major Clash Royale updates that caused community uproar today at Gamescom Dev.
Playing on some of the more extreme feedback the Clash Royale team has received recently, game design lead James Back declared: “At the end of last year, we killed Clash Royale”.
He also admitted that, after several months of fierce, negative player reaction, Back sat at his desk wondering: “How did we misjudge this so badly? Like, how did we get this quite so wrong…?”
Game design lead Back and community manager Emilia Russell then talked through some of the game updates that caused the player discontent, and what they learned from it all.
points: Game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell talked through Clash Royale player drama and how to deal with it at Gamescom Dev.
